overall_reason: A small, specific page for one wine bar: real opening nights, 140 bottles, a £25 monthly tasting and an honest unconnected form, set in a dark serif mood that suits a place open only after five; its weak spots are missing facts and two thin sub-lines, not a stock skeleton.

findings.where: list section, tasting section and Find us footer, all widths
findings.evidence: Three dashed missing-fact slots on one page: "The full list: link to come.", "The next date is to be announced.", "Address to be announced". The data_slots detector did not count them because they are not literal [DATA NEEDED] text.
findings.before: "link to come" / "to be announced" / "Address to be announced"
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: street address] at minimum; publish the list link and the next tasting date, or cut the list link until it exists
findings.why: More than two slots means the page was built before its content existed; the page's two jobs (come in, book a tasting) both end at a missing fact.

findings.evidence: Heading "Find us after five." at display size is followed only by "Address to be announced" and two footer links; the hero's secondary CTA "Find us" and the nav item both land here.
findings.before: "Find us after five." + "Address to be announced"
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: street address, nearest station, map link]; until then drop the "Find us" CTA from the hero and nav
findings.why: A section whose heading promises a place and gives none reads as a template slot; the visitor who clicks "Find us" learns nothing.

findings.evidence: Failed T-RIVAL-NAME and T-THREE-LINE: "The bar / Open a bottle and stay." and "The shop / Take one home." stay true for any wine bar with a retail shelf; neither line is picturable to this place or falsifiable.
findings.before: "Open a bottle and stay." / "Take one home."
findings.after: One concrete fact each, e.g. [DATA NEEDED: corkage or by-the-glass detail for the bar; shop price range or takeaway discount]
findings.why: Two equal headings with four-word sub-lines are the only filler on an otherwise specific page.

findings.evidence: Static text "Open tonight from 5pm" sits in the header, while the hours table says Monday to Wednesday are "Closed". The capture shows no script making it conditional.
findings.after: Compute it from the day ("Open tonight from 5pm" / "Closed tonight, open Thursday"), or replace with the fixed "Thu to Sun from 5pm"
findings.why: A status line that is false three nights a week is invented state, and it is the first fact many visitors read.

findings.where: h1 "Natural wine after five." vs h2 "Four nights a week, Thursday to Sunday.", 1440
findings.evidence: The hours h2 renders at the same 84px as the h1 (sweep flat_hierarchy hit) and, being two long lines, is visually heavier than the hero on tile 2.
findings.after: Set the hours h2 to --text-section (clamp(2rem, 2.5vw + 1rem, 3.5rem)) like the other h2s
findings.why: Context for the sweep hit: the hours line out-shouts the hero, so the page has two first reads.

strengths: Hours shown as a seven-day row with closed days dimmed and the open run marked by a rule: a fact turned into the page's most specific visual.
Concrete numbers that only this bar can say: 140 bottles, four nights, £25 a place, once a month.
The email form fails honestly: "Nothing was sent: this form is not connected yet."
Dark warm palette, Young Serif display and one salmon accent fit a bar that opens after five; it reads as a chosen mood, not the neon dark-single-accent default.
Photo credits with licences in the footer.
not_investigated: Photography: all three Wikimedia images were blocked in capture; the gradient frames are fallbacks, not design choices, so T-DELETION on imagery was not judged.
Fonts were shimmed (Young Serif, Instrument Sans); the render is assumed close to intended.
